Dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

Recent findings suggest that england head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Industry observers note that chelsea have two substantial chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

In a recent development, boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

In a recent development, the Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Industry observers note that there has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

Recent findings suggest that at 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

Sources indicate that how has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Industry observers note that brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

In a recent development, the hosts have their second inside the opening quarter of an hour. Rogers does well on the left side of the box to hold off Vuskovic before squaring the ball. Neto runs across Kadioglu’s blindside and pokes home first time from eight yards out. Kadioglu should really have dealt with that and was too flat-footed. He should not have allowed Neto to get to that ball first.

The travelling Brighton fans are making sure that Pedro knows what they think of their former player.

Up in the stands, England boss Thomas Tuchel is sat next to Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, both former Chelsea bosses.

According to recent reports, since the start of the 2024/25 season, no goalkeeper in the Premier League has made more errors leading to goals than Verbruggen’s 10. Second on that list; Sanchez, who is not in the Chelsea squad today.

Brighton win their first corner of the afternoon and Martinez is forced into action, punching away at his near post as the delivery threatened to creep in.

Sources indicate that that is an absolute gift for the home side after a huge error from Brighton. Pedro flicks on at the near post and Wieffer makes the block near his own line. Verbruggen then tries to catch the loose ball but he and Wieffer end up getting into each others’ way. The ball then falls to Lavia, who pokes home. As they did at Craven Cottage the other night, Chelsea hit the front early.

In a recent development, there was a fist pump from Chelsea’s latest set-piece coach Austin MacPhee after Romeo Lavia’s goal from the corner. It looks like MacPhee will be claiming credit for that one, even though it came thanks to an error from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen. Xabi Alonso also celebrated with MacPhee.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

He might be trying to sell his shares in Chelsea, but co-owner Todd Boehly is at today’s game in the Stamford Bridge stands.

Before we get going, Stamford Bridge pays tribute to Bobby Tambling and Ken Bates, who both died over the summer. Wreaths are laid in their memory with their families carrying framed pictures of the two men.

Emiliano Martínez turns 34 on September 2 and by most tangible metrics, the goalkeeper is past his peak.

But it is the intangibles that set Martínez apart and why his availability at a knock-down price from Aston Villa convinced Chelsea to seize a market opportunity.

At £7.5m, Martínez could prove to be Chelsea’s smartest piece of business of the summer and there is little doubt he will be box-office at Stamford Bridge.

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso mentioned. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”.

In a recent development, brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

In a recent development, “When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

According to recent reports, “We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”.

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1310 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.
  • Industry observers note that that is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.

It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.

Industry observers note that that is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for. The manner of his side’s capitulation - and the substitutions he made - in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium last July enraged the nation, but Tuchel stated the fault was in the damned DNA of the English, that we were underlings, and that our players found it constitutionally impossible to keep hold of the ball.

Whatever Tuchel thinks, the fact remains that the tie against Lamine Yamal, Fabian Ruiz, Pedri and Mikel Oyarzabal and the rest of the world champions at the home of Atletico Madrid offers Tuchel and his players the opportunity to encourage themselves and their fans that they are not destined to be also-rans wired to fall at the final hurdle for evermore.

Spain are formidable opposition. They are on a record-breaking run of 43 matches unbeaten and have won their last 12 in succession. They haven't drawn a game since their June 15 game against Cape Verde in the World Cup. Their last defeat was on March 22, 2024, when they lost 1-0 to Colombia in a friendly. Some ask whether they are the best international side the world has ever seen.

‘Spain seem unbeatable,’ Tuchel said, when he walked into the press room at the Metropolitano on Saturday night and heard hymns of praise being lavished upon the opponents he is about to face.

‘They have a very strong identity and a very strong mentality. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are up for the fight. We are up for a spectacular match. We can see how far we can push the limits with the world champions in Madrid. The group is full of self-belief and rightly so.’.

England must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - even if they have flaws.

Thomas Tuchel must show he can find a way around the limitations presented by the 'DNA' he has complained about.

This may be the toughest game that Tuchel’s England side play until the European Championships in 2028, where the final will be contested at Wembley, and they will play all their games at home. They need to go into that tournament with the belief that they can beat the best when the pressure is at its highest.

Beating Spain away in the final game of the group phase of the Nations League is not quite the same as a critical match at a major tournament but it is as stiff a challenge as Tuchel is going to face until then. Beating Croatia 7-0 in front of gangs of schoolkids in Rijeka last month was hailed as the best England performance of the Tuchel era. Which says it all, really.

It was a great performance in a relatively meaningless match. Now it is time for him to show that he can marshal an England side to succeed against the very best, not fall apart when the prize is in sight. His protestations of powerlessness in the aftermath of the Argentina defeat were not a good look for a coach who was hired with the idea that his coaching prowess and his game management could get England over the line.

Has he learned anything from the manner of the Argentina defeat? ‘This game against Spain will be proof of concept at the highest level,’ he mentioned, ‘but we are up for it. I think we have taken the next step after the World Cup. The best thing is to trust our process and trust ourselves. We need to be clear about how we want to impose ourselves and I think that is all visible.’.

Now it is time for him to show that he can find a way past the limitations of England’s footballing DNA, find a way to compete with Spain and France when it really matters, and find a way to end the culture of near misses that has come to be England’s lot in the last decade of appearances in semi-finals and finals.

England have played six matches since that day of crushing disappointment in Atlanta and scored 22 goals. But in the only one of those matches that really mattered, they lost 3-2 to Spain at Wembley in the opening tie of their Nations League campaign at the end of September, a game in which they were largely outclassed by Luis de la Fuente’s team.

Industry observers note that spain are what England have to aim for. Tuchel mentioned their example and their ability and their mindset straight after the semi-final loss to Argentina. ‘Ball possession plays a crucial role,’ he mentioned at his post-match press conference in Atlanta. ‘It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in our Spanish DNA or in our Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball.’.

This may well be their toughest game until the final of the 2028 European Championships, if they get that far.

The England coach said more recently that England need to go back to trusting a traditional style that emphasises direct, high-intensity physicality rather than trying to copy Spanish patience in ball-retention. England, though, were taught a lesson in sophistication by the Spanish in September.

And for all the attention lavished on Yamal, Spain’s defence is the best in the world. Rodri, the shield for that defence and also the world’s best in the role, is not fit for this game but even without him, Spain’s back-line inspires an awful lot more confidence than England’s.

Industry observers note that ‘They were the best in the World Cup at the back,’ Declan Rice, England’s central midfielder, said on Saturday. ‘Defence wins you titles. Everyone talks about their attacking talent but you look at their central defenders, their full backs and the way their midfielders contribute to the defence, too.’.

That defence will have to stop England’s resurgent front line, led by Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who could be flanked by Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers and backed up by the supreme talent of Jude Bellingham just behind them.

According to recent reports, bellingham’s improving relationship with Tuchel, which cannot have been harmed by the inclusion of Bellingham’s brother, Jobe, in this squad, is another reason to hope that England still retain the capacity to improve after the World Cup. The elder Bellingham has become England’s most influential player.

England at their best would be one of the few teams capable of extending them. Rice stated on Saturday that the game between the two sides was ‘massive’. England need to prove they can find a way to get closer to the world champions. To beat them, Rice said, would be a ‘massive statement’.

‘Playing against them is a great incentive to win. It will show where we are as a group. We are trying to attack teams full throttle and with players like Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers in our attack, it feels as if it is going to take off one night and maybe tomorrow night will be the night. We can beat Spain. For sure, we can.’.

Sources indicate that tuchel needs to prove England can win, not just be noble contenders. They need to prove that their DNA need not be a curse.

Almost €800m was spent among Bundesliga clubs on signings in the summer, per Transfermarkt, but while Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have splashed significant on Ismael Saibari and Konstantinos Karetsas, there’s been some excellent signings throughout the 18 teams.

Get German Football News explores the five best….

Recent findings suggest that flourishing at RB Leipzig since returning to the club on loan in the summer, Christopher Nkunku has returned five goals and provided two assists since returning to the Saxony club. The Frenchman provided an assist against Borussia Mönchengladbach on his second debut before opening his account at the Red Bull Arena in Leipzig’s 5-0 victory over Hamburg. The 29-year-old then struck a hat-trick against Eintracht Frankfurt before adding a goal and assist to his 2026/27 tally against Augsburg prior to the international break. Often starting in a three-pronged attack alongside Romulo and Antonio Nusa/Tidiam Gomis, Nkunku is given the freedom to roam by Martin Demichelis, which makes his a nuisance for opposition defenders. Ranked in the 95th percentile for xGoals on target (4.14), Nkunku has proved clinical in front of goal, scoring five of his eight attempts on target.

The Spaniard has substantial boots to fill following the departure of Alejandro Grimaldo, but the former Napoli man is settling into life at Bayer Leverkusen just fine. The 25-year-old has scored one goal and created a further four in his nine Bundesliga starts since swapping Italy for Germany. Equally adept at playing as the left-sided centre-back in a back three, or as the left-back or left-wing back in a back four/five, no defender ranks higher in the Bundesliga than Gutiérrez for assists and big chances created (eight) in Germany’s top flight this season.

Hennes Behrens at €3.5m is proving to be a steal for Augsburg, who are proving to be one of the Bundesliga’s best recruiters. Joining from Hoffenheim after spending last season on loan at Heidenheim, the 21-year-old is proving a useful weapon from left-back, where he’s registered three assists in nine Bundesliga outings this term. Possessing explosive pace and pinpoint crossing, Behrens is fast becoming one of the league’s most useful full-backs in the final third.

It has been revealed that re-joining Werder Bremen on loan after a failed spell abroad, Niclas Füllkrug is firing on all cylinders back at the Weserstadion. The 33-year-old sits at the top of the Bundesliga’s scoring charts this term having scored nine goals in as many appearances – seven of those have come from set-piece situations. Playing with a smile on his face once again, it’s great to see Füllkrug back to his best, which has also seen him return to the German national team. Carry on, and Bremen could well be competing for a place in Europe if the veteran goal-getter remains injury free and keeps up his output.

Joining newly promoted Elversberg from Bayern Munich having spent last season on loan at 2. Bundesliga side Hertha Berlin, Maurice Krattenmacher has scored four goals and provided one assist in nine Bundesliga games this season – of which he’s only started four. The 21-year-old came off the bench to score a brace against Gladbach to secure a dramatic 4-3 victory for Vincent Wagner’s side, before netting against Bayern the following matchday with a superb curling effort. The attacking-midfielder also registered an assist and scored in wins of Augsburg and Mainz as the Bundesliga newcomers enjoy a magnificent start to their Bundesliga tenure.

In his first press conference back from his illness-related absence, Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany offered an interesting perspective on Jamal Musiala’s impending return to competitive football. The Belgian suggested that the German international could benefit from the changing expectations surrounding him. Speaking at Thursday’s pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s Bundesliga encounter with Köln, Kompany also addressed recent remarks from honorary president Uli Hoeneß concerning the 23-year-old’s long-term prospects.

According to recent reports, musiala is expected to return to Bayern’s matchday squad on Friday, provided he encounters no setbacks during Thursday’s final training session. The attacking midfielder has been sidelined since suffering a significant thigh injury while warming up for Germany’s UEFA Nations League encounter with the Netherlands in September.

Recent findings suggest that the latest setback interrupted an encouraging return to competitive football. Musiala has accumulated approximately 200 minutes this season, scoring in both of his starts. He opened the scoring in Bayern’s 5-0 Champions League victory over Bodø/Glimt and the 7-0 Bundesliga triumph over Union Berlin.

Musiala’s recovery has attracted additional attention following recent remarks from Uli Hoeneß questioning whether the midfielder can regain his previous performance level. Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen also raised questions about how the club might respond if Musiala’s performances were permanently affected. Sporting director Max Eberl sought to reassure supporters on Thursday, emphasizing the club’s continued belief in Musiala’s ability to rediscover his best form.

Kompany, meanwhile, adopted a different approach to the discussion. Rather than disagreeing with Bayern’s hierarchy, the Belgian emphasized that his responsibility as head coach requires him to maintain confidence in his players regardless of the concerns expressed elsewhere within the organization.

The Bayern trainer also suggested that Musiala’s changed circumstances could provide valuable motivation. Having previously enjoyed the status of an almost untouchable young star, the midfielder now has an opportunity to demonstrate his abilities without carrying precisely the same expectations.

Kompany drew a parallel between Musiala’s comeback and his own return following an extended absence due to illness. The coach expressed hope that both experiences could provide renewed energy for Bayern during the remainder of the season. The 40-year-old also praised Musiala’s determination throughout his rehabilitation, emphasizing that the youngster must ultimately demonstrate his recovery through performances on the pitch.

It has been revealed that “We don’t have differing opinions,” Kompany added when questioned about Hoeneß’ comments on Musiala. “What we have is different roles. My role is to believe in all the players. That’s my role. It would be a catastrophe if I came here and stated that, for example, five specific players didn’t matter.”.

In a recent development, “The fact that we have different roles is one of the things that function well at Bayern,” Kompany continued. “I have 100 percent respect for the opinions of the [club] hierarchy. I don’t have a problem with that. One has to put it into perspective and we can also utilize this in a sporting sense.”.

Sources indicate that “There’s nothing that can serve as a greater motivation for a player like Jamal,” Kompany concluded. “There’s something he can show without the same pressure as when he was a ‘golden child’. This is also a nice moment. Luckily, the head coach has had plenty of such moments in his career and I’m looking forward to it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has revealed that he deliberately refrained from making any coaching decisions during his recent absence, insisting that assistant coach Aaron Danks and the remaining staff deserved complete responsibility for the team. Speaking at Thursday’s press conference ahead of his return to the touchline against Cologne, the 40-year-old offered an interesting insight into his management philosophy and reflected on watching his team succeed from a distance.

Danks assumed responsibility for Bayern’s first team after Kompany collapsed during a reserve-team training session on October 23. The Belgian required hospitalization and an extended period away from his coaching duties. Bayern nevertheless maintained their unbeaten run under Danks, recording four victories and one draw across five competitive fixtures.

The results included a 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Freiburg, a 6-1 DFB-Pokal triumph against Magdeburg, a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund, a 2-0 Champions League win away at Atlético Madrid, and a 2-1 victory over Mainz.

Kompany emphasized that he had deliberately avoided interfering with his assistants’ decision-making throughout the period. Although he maintained contact with the coaching staff and discussed matches afterward, the Belgian insisted that his involvement was limited to understanding their decisions rather than influencing them. The arrangement reflected his conviction that stepping away from responsibility required allowing those taking his place to exercise genuine authority.

In a recent development, kompany also expressed particular satisfaction with Bayern’s Champions League victory over Atlético Madrid. Watching his players support one another and overcome the Spanish side without him on the touchline represented one of the most memorable experiences of his coaching career. The period away from daily responsibilities also afforded Kompany an unusual opportunity for reflection.

Industry observers note that the Bayern trainer suggested that coaches rarely receive the chance to consider their work from a fresh perspective without leaving their clubs. Although his absence was involuntary, he nevertheless found time to consider how Bayern might improve further upon his return.

“I didn’t make a single decision. Zero,” Kompany emphasized when discussing his absence at Thursday’s press conference. “But there’s an key reason why I wasn’t involved in that decision-making process. You must respect the work. You can’t be there every day, then suddenly not be there anymore, and still insist on having an opinion and making decisions. You simply can’t do that.”.

According to recent reports, “Ultimately, the best place to be is on the bench with the team,” the Bayern coach continued. “But I also enjoyed seeing how the lads stuck together. That really was one of the highlights of my career. As a coach, you never get the chance to have a reboot, a fresh start in your career at the same club. Usually, you have to do that somewhere else. In my case, that’s a luxury I now have.”.

Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026.

A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.

Industry observers note that on Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) declared Keith Cooper had died aged 78. But he is alive and well.

The news reached the ears of the Wembley Cup final referee when he went out to his local sports centre for a flu jab only to be told: 'You were dead.'.

The Football Association of Wales posted a statement online and a tribute on social media to announce his death, but then withdrew it within an hour.

Mr Cooper, who is the father of former Nottingham Forest and Leicester boss Steve Cooper, told a Welsh sports website: 'I walked into the sports centre yesterday to have my jab and the fellow went, "You were dead!".

'Well, I'm not dead, I'm here and I'm OK!'.

The blunder appears to have emerged after the Wiltshire FA declared the death of another referee called Keith Cooper, who the football chiefs in Wales believed was the other Keith Cooper.

The FAW statement noted: 'Keith was a well-known figure who enjoyed an exceptional career at both domestic and international level and would later hold the position of FAW Referees' Officer following his retirement in 1996.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) announced Keith Cooper had died aged 78.

Mark Beeney goalkeeper of Leeds United is Sent Off of by Referee Keith A Cooper for hand ball outside the area during the Premier League match between Manchester United and Leeds United at Old Trafford on April 17, 1996 in Manchester, England.

Former professional football John Fashanu is pictured with referee Keith Cooper during a Wimbledon F.C. match.

'Born and raised in Pontypridd, he is considered one of Wales' best match officials through his highly-regarded status in the game.

'In addition to his work with FAW, Keith was also a valued member of the Wiltshire FA Council who recognised his 'integrity, passion and commitment' in their tribute to his services to the game.

'Everyone at the FAW sends their condolences to his family and friends at this sad time.'.

Mr Cooper oversaw the 1994 League Cup final between Aston Villa and Manchester United, won by Villa 3-1, and worked in radio punditry after hanging up his whistle.

The FAW has not issued an explanation over the posted tribute. His family has not yet commented on the error.

But the unfortunate mistake has not spared the FAW from ridicule by other football fans.

One remarked: 'We always said there was only one Keith Cooper - turns out there are two.'.

Another said: 'Glad the whistle wasn't blown too early on Keith and much respect to the family of the other one.'.

Produce vino da una decina d’anni e nelle Langhe ha il suo campo base, chiamato «Ca’ del profeta».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Niko Kovac had an unusual concern to contend with ahead of Borussia Dortmund’s return to Bundesliga action: the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Asked at Thursday’s press conference whether the eagerly anticipated video game had become a major topic inside the BVB dressing room, Kovac joked that he hoped none of his players had been staying up deep into the night playing it.

The Dortmund head coach conceded that several members of his squad were likely already heavily involved with the game, quipping that he hoped they would not “confuse day and night” ahead of Saturday’s trip to Borussia Mönchengladbach.

The light-hearted exchange came at the end of a press conference otherwise dominated by Dortmund’s need to hit the ground running following the international break.

In a recent development, BVB travel to bottom-of-the-table Gladbach on Saturday at 15:30 CET with 21 points from their opening nine Bundesliga matches. Kovac’s side remain unbeaten in league play and sit second, level on points with leaders Bayern Munich. Dortmund have also conceded only seven goals, the best defensive record in the division.

Industry observers note that “We can’t afford to take any time to get going,” Kovac noted. “There are still eight games left this year. In these games, we want to cement our place at the top of the Bundesliga. The other teams are pushing from behind. We have to be ready right away.”.

Industry observers note that saturday’s match begins another demanding stretch for Dortmund. BVB face eight competitive fixtures in 29 days before the winter break, having only just completed a run of nine matches across 29 of days prior to the November international break.

The experience of the previous international break also provides an obvious warning.

Dortmund failed to win any of their first three matches after returning to club action in October, drawing 2-2 with Werder Bremen and 0-0 with Union Berlin in the Bundesliga either side of a 1-0 Champions League defeat to Bodø/Glimt.

Kovac nevertheless believes the circumstances are somewhat different this time. The Dortmund coach noted that the latest international window involved a more conventional two-match schedule rather than the unusually heavy international programme surrounding the previous break, leaving his players closer to their normal competitive rhythm.

Getting into matches more quickly has become an increasingly prominent theme for Dortmund. BVB’s last ten Bundesliga goals have all arrived after half-time, an unusual run that Kovac would preferably bring to an end in Gladbach.

“If you take an early lead, the game opens up much more swiftly,” Kovac said.

Recent findings suggest that the trend has done little damage to Dortmund’s results so far, but it has repeatedly forced BVB to remain patient before finding breakthroughs. Five of their nine Bundesliga matches this season have reached half-time without Dortmund scoring.

Kovac will also have several late personnel decisions to make. Serhou Guirassy, Waldemar Anton, and Carney Chukwuemeka remained in Dortmund during the international break while dealing with muscular problems. Kovac stated that their availability would be assessed ahead of the weekend and stressed that “nothing is ruled out.”.

Samuele Inacio has meanwhile returned from international duty carrying a minor complaint, leaving another question mark over Dortmund’s squad for Saturday.

The mood became considerably lighter when Kovac was questioned about the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

A reporter asked whether the Dortmund coach had encountered an unusual number of players requesting a “sick day” following the game’s release and whether GTA had become a major topic inside the dressing room. Kovac was also asked whether he owned a PlayStation 5 himself.

Sources indicate that “I don’t have one,” Kovac responded. “I reached the age at which I’m out. I believe I heard or read some time ago that this game was coming out. I hope my lads haven’t been playing deep into the night. How does one do something like that these days? Per App or does one need hardware [a gaming console]?”.

The reporter clarified that the game could be downloaded on a console, adding that BVB striker Fabio Silva had commented on downloading it in the three days since its release.

“Okay, then I’ll act on the assumption that they [the players] are playing it,” Kovac continued. “I hope they don’t play it so excessively that they can’t tell day from night anymore. That could be problematic. But today is a wonderful day not just because of the fact that this game is being released, but because we also have two in-house birthdays with Costa [Konstantinos Karetsas] and Joey [Veerman].

Recent findings suggest that “That’s much more notable than this game,” Kovac concluded. “But I have heard that a few [of the players] are intensively involved [with the video game].”.

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

According to recent reports, in the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “fresh signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT.

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s significant project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the complications in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Recent findings suggest that harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k.

According to recent reports, united were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Industry observers note that rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

In a recent development, bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD.

Sources indicate that after missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR.

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

According to recent reports, “There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick stated. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”.

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

It has been revealed that he recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

In a recent development, asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”.

It has been revealed that the Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

It has been revealed that “We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”.

In a recent development, and on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He revealed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

In a recent development, “There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”.

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

Industry observers note that “But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”.

It has been revealed that the hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

In a recent development, “Scoring before half-time is always vital if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

Recent findings suggest that “Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick mentioned: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

It has been revealed that “So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”.

It has been revealed that against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

Ligue 1 outfit AS Monaco have reached an agreement with German youth international Paris Brunner (20) regarding a contract extension beyond 2028, according to RMC Sport, as reported via our colleagues at Get French Football News.

The young attacker is expected to sign a contract through to 2030 after scoring eight goals and providing one assists in 13 matches for Monaco in 2026/27 after joining the Principality club from Borussia Dortmund in the summer in search of senior football, having not made an appearance for BVB’s first team.

Brunner’s performances also coincided with a run in Antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21 squad during the recent international break where he featured in defeats against Belgium and Croatia. He was, though, one of the winners in Germany’s youth team, which also saw the youngster earn praise from Di Salvo. “Moving Paris [to the left] was something that we wanted as we wanted to have a player like that on the left [wing]. It paid off on our second goal,” he explained.

Brajan Gruda scored two goals and provided two assists in his first two appearances for the German national team against Serbia and the Netherlands over the recent international break and with four assists in seven Bundesliga games for RB Leipzig in 2026/27, the 22-year-old’s stock continues to rise.

On loan from Premier League side Brighton and Hove Albion, Gruda’s move to Leipzig will become permanent in the upcoming year if he plays every match between now and Hoffenheim on 16 January. The fee: €25m. The newly capped German international will then pen a contract until July 2031, without a release clause.

It has been revealed that that ultimately means that Leipzig can command any fee they wish for their rising star. With interest from Liverpool and Bayern Munich, and with no intention of selling, BILD estimate Leipzig’s valuation of Gruda to be around €100m.

With impressive numbers across his first two Germany appearances, Gruda was naturally one of seven winners in Jürgen Klopp’s November squad.

Provstgaard e Isaksen hanno giocato entrambi tutti i 99 minuti con la Danimarca. Il difensore ha retto l’urto, mentre Isaksen ha servito un assist. In Nations League, però, i danesi si sono fatti rimontare dalla Norvegia.

A dismayed mother and father spoke out after their 'elite' athlete twin sons were arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as they returned to their Alabama college.

Wallace State Community College soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, 19, were taken into ICE custody after a traffic stop on November 4 while on their way to campus, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

The Venezuelan twins were returning from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta, in Georgia when they were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer during a traffic stop in east-central Alabama.

The brothers graduated from Lawrenceville's Archer High School after a successful varsity soccer career that included a first ever region title for the school.

'This is the house of two elite soccer players,' Carlos Enrique Orta, their father, told the outlet.

Luis and Carlos are asylum seekers who applied for protections after legally entering the US on a tourist visa, like their parents.

That visa expired and the twins were granted US work permits and Georgia driver's licenses, according to the outlet.

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, told the Daily Mail on Saturday that the brothers had legally entered the US with permission to stay on a temporary basis on June 21, 2022, but then 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws.'.

Twin brothers and soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, both 19, were taken into ICE custody on November 5 after being arrested the previous day.

Luis and Carlos were region title-winning soccer players for Archer High School in Lawrenceville, Georgia.

The brothers were arrested as they returned from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta (both left).

The DHS spokesperson told the Daily Mail: 'All their claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and they will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law.'.

'To be clear, pending applications do NOT confer legal status,' the statement continued.

Carlos was named the offensive player of the year and Luis the midfield player of the year by their high school this year.

They had received soccer scholarships to attend Wallace State, which they began doing this fall, but now face deportation to Venezuela.

'It's been hell,' Santoro de Orta, their mother, told the outlet.

She added that she supported ICE 'taking away the criminals' but said her children did not fit that description.

A final decision on the brothers' asylum case is still pending as they remain in custody.

The concerned mother claimed police mentioned the twins' car had failed to come to a complete stop at a stop sign.

The brothers were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer as they were returning to Wallace State Community College, where they have soccer scholarships.

Sources indicate that the family applied for asylum protections after legally entering the country on a tourist visa. The DHS said the brothers 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws'.

The Lincoln Police Department signed a partnership agreement with ICE in July.

ICE remarked the program allows trained local officers to exercise limited immigration authority during routine police work under federal supervision, according to the Cullman Tribune.

Luis and Carlos were booked into the Talladega County Jail on November 4 and transferred to ICE custody the following day.

Their father, Orta, described how the family was grappling with guilt as they shared what happened to their children.

In a recent development, 'If anyone is at fault, it's me. It's us,' Orta told the outlet. 'Because I insist and I will continue to insist that Carlos and Luis came here because of a decision we made.'.

Sources indicate that he added: 'Carlos and Luis stayed here because of a decision from mom and dad. Carlos and Luis are here because of us.'.

The Santoro twins were taken to the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana after their arrest, WABE reported.

The brothers have been taken to the the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana.

It has been revealed that the Lincoln Police Department signed an partnership agreement with ICE in July. A department officer arrested the brothers.

A friend of the twins, Nicolas Azcarate Florez, remarked he had spoken to them multiple times since they were taken into custody.

'They've been saying that they've been moved five times, so it has been difficult for them,' Azcarate Florez told the outlet.

Azcarate Florez said the brothers were 'players that you could just give the ball to, and you would know that they would do something good with it.'.

'If we needed them, we would know that they would be there to help us out of a sticky situation,' he added.

The brothers were taken into custody on the same week that the Republican Party faced a historic blue wave in the midterm elections that was seen as a rebuke of the GOP's immigration policy.

One of President Donald Trump's first moves afterwards was to name Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

Miller, one of Trump's most loyal and longest-serving advisers going back to his first administration, is known for his hardline views on immigration.

Critics have cited Miller as the architect of some of Trump's most divisive policies, including separating migrant families during deportations in the President's first term.

Ethan Nwaneri (19) registered two assists in England U21s recent 3-2 victory over France, but the Borussia Dortmund man has struggled for playing time in the Bundesliga recently.

Sources indicate that speaking at Thursday’s press conference, BVB head coach Niko Kovač weighed in on the player’s situation. “We have very good players in those positions up front, he explained. Nwaneri initially replaced Giannis Konstantelias, who suffered an ACL injury on his Bundesliga debut against Hamburg, while Fabio Silva is shining alongside Serhou Guirassy, while Konstantinos Karetsas has recently returned from a back injury.

“The competition is tough,” added Kovač, who did praise Nwaneri’s performances for England. “As far as Ethan is concerned, we’re delighted,” he remarked. ” It was a friendly match and he did really well.”.

With an assist to his name on his Bundesliga but against Hoffenheim on Matchday 2, Nwaneri has featured in eight of nine possible league games, playing 336 minutes for Die Schwarzgelben in Germany’s top flight.

Dopo le votazioni di giugno che avevano fatto prevalere il nome di Giovanni Malagò, una nuova chiamata alle urne è stata resa necessaria dal commissariamento della Federazione per via di un mancato tesseramento dello stesso Malagò che dunque ha, sostanzialmente, invalidato i risultati dei primi voti. It has been revealed that il commento di Beppe Accardi su diversi temi tra cui l'elezione del presidente FIGC tra Galliani e Malagò: "Nazionale? Per costruire le cose c'è bisogno di tempo e lavorare. Sappiamo che dobbiamo iniziare un nuovo ciclo, purtroppo siamo diventati un paese in tutti i settori dove vige la polemica continua. Non si cerca di risolvere i problemi, ma di trovare dei colpevoli" Così a TuttoMercatoWeb.com l'operatore di mercato Beppe Accardi a proposito dell'Italia e l'eliminazione dalla Nations League. Elezioni FIGC? Galliani tutta la vita. Parliamo di un uomo di calcio. Sono felice per la Lazio e per Gattuso, è la prova che lavorare in silenzio senza chiacchiere e polemiche porta dei risultati".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich maintained their unbeaten start to the season but had to come from behind to secure a share of the spoils against struggling Cologne with Nathaniel Brown cancelling out Mikey Moore’s first-half strike.

The substantial news coming into Friday’s Matchday 10 curtain-raiser was Vincent Kompany’s return to the touchline, one month after he collapsed at the club’s training ground.

Bayern remained unchanged following their 2-1 victory against Mainz prior to the international break, but the notable inclusion on the bench was 19-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora, who was named in Bayern’s matchday squad for the first time, while Cologne made once change after their 2-1 derby defeat against Bayer Leverkusen, with Luka Lochoshvili coming into defence for attacker Marius Bülter.

It has been revealed that michael Olise threatened early on for the hosts, but it was Cologne who took an early lead at the Allianz Arena. Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore opened his Bundesliga account for the season in the 12th minute, rounding Jonas Urbig and slotting into an empty net. It then went from bad to worse for Bayern when Harry Kane was forced off with what looked to be an ankle injury.

Bayern’s equaliser arrived in the 37th minute when Nathaniel Brown struck from a central position just outside of the area, stroking the ball into the bottom corner past Marvin Schwäbe to level proceedings heading into the interval.

After colliding with Cologne’s Tom Krauß in the first half, Olise remained in the dressing room at the break, with Kompany awarding Tim Binder his Bundesliga debut, as their injuries continued to mount up with Serge Gnabry and Luis Díaz already sidelined.

Sources indicate that shortly after the break, Moore came close to adding to his tally but was denied by Urbig from close range before Lennart Karl, who had been quiet in the first period, fired just wide minutes later. Urbig was called into action again, first to deny Remarked El Mala after a dizzying-run from Moore on the hour mark, before Linton Maina’s well struck follow-up volley stung the palms of the Bayern stopper – who is yet to keep a clean sheet this season.

According to recent reports, both teams had chances to win it in the dying embers. Jamal Musiala, returning from injury, placed the ball just the wrong side of the post after superb play from Josip Stanišić and Karl before El Mala placed his shot from close-range agonisingly wide at the other end following Sebastian Sebulonsen’s cross.

The result keeps Bayern top of the Bundesliga, but Borussia Dortmund can climb above the leaders with a win against Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday, while Cologne remain winless in five Bundesliga games.

Bayern Munich: Urbig (7) – Laimer (5), Upamecano (6), Tah (6), Stanišić (5) – Kimmich (6), Pavlović (5), Karl (5), Olise (5), Brown (6) – Kane (-).

Others: Bischof (7), Binder (5), Musiala (-), Kim (-), Codjo-Evora (-).

Cologne: Schwäbe (6) – Simpson-Pusey (6), Schmied (5), Lochoshvili (6) – Sebulonsen (6), Okon-Engstler (6), Krauß (7), Sosa (6), Maina (6), Moore (7) – S. El Mala (6).

Others: Thielmann (-), Jóhannesson (-), Heskey (), Castro-Montes (), Bülter ().

In a recent development, the Englishman opened his Bundesliga account for the season with an outstanding, composed finish past Jonas Urbig. Showing clear development at Cologne, the 19-year-old almost added a second shortly after the break, but wasn’t able to generate enough power on his effort from close range, which was collected by Bayern’s custodian.

Industry observers note that oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

In a recent development, lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless Newly introduced Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

According to recent reports, where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

Industry observers note that and yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Recent findings suggest that today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Recent findings suggest that messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

According to recent reports, you struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

It has been revealed that as a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose.

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

Industry observers note that that alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

Hamilton Academical 1 Ross County 2.

The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving Latest Douglas Park.

The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe. There may, however, be a positive prognosis.

Accies, despite their defeat, are whispering about stability, even though ‘legacy debt’ has to be faced, perhaps contested.

County, meanwhile, will not say it even in a whisper but Saturday’s victory takes them eight points clear at the top and heavily fancied for the title. The Staggies have one set of hooves in the Championship.

Scottish football, of course, does not restrict itself to the cliched fare of top of the table clashes so New Douglas Park hosted a striker who is 39 later this month, a winger who was once a Scottish international, and a gentleman in the stands who once played against George Best. And a Ross County fan who regularly travels up from North Wales.

These exotic avenues demand to be explored but perennial questions about the financial health of the Accies had to be asked, too, after reports this week stating that hospitality packages at the club were being suspended.

An Accies fan feels the pain of defeat during Saturday's home loss to Ross County.

Allan Currie, chairman, answered them over a half-time pie.

‘We have come on in leaps and bounds but every week seems to throw up different challenges,’ he remarked. ‘We have a level of debt that we have inherited and we are working with the creditors to try to navigate our way through that.’.

Matters on the field are positive, despite Saturday’s defeat.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The guys on the pitch, manager, and his staff have been unbelievable. Surviving in this league last season was phenomenal given what they were going through but it couldn’t be better now,’ he said. ‘Off the pitch, we are fighting with the different challenges we have. We are in a much better place even if we are not out the woods yet.’.

Asked what the level of pressure on him, he stated: ‘I am the guy on the ground but Rob Edwards is carrying out negotiations.’.

Recent findings suggest that edwards, through his Morley Group, took over the club earlier this year but has been sideswiped by a number of claims for payment. However, Currie has faith in the owner.

‘Without him, the club would not survive. Rob should take all the credit,’ he stated.

Asked what the short-term aims for the club were, Currie replied with a smile: ‘A goal in the second half would be good.’ A goal was scored but not for the Accies.

But the club remain in second place and the play-offs seem a more than reasonable prospect.

Ross County goalscorer Kieran Phillips battles with Hamilton's Kai Smutek.

It has been revealed that with 10 minutes to go, Hamilton brought on their latest signing. Barrie McKay, who has played for Scotland and scored for Rangers in a Scottish Cup semi-final against Celtic. His considerable achievements, though, paled in comparison to the subject of a casual conversation in the bar before the match.

‘I played against George Best,’ noted Alan McDougall, with an air so off-hand one could have believed he was merely ordering another pint.

In a recent development, ‘Yes, I played 200 games for the Accies. Davie McParland brought me here as a 21-year-old and I played for about six years. I went to Stranraer for a year and then went down south. I played against Best with the Accies.’.

Sources indicate that the Northern Irish genius played for Hibernian in 1979-80. ‘He was well past his best and that was sad,’ remarked McDougall. Best’s addiction to alcohol had taken a severe toll.

‘I came back to watch games five or six years ago,’ noted McDougall. ‘When the club went to Clyde, it destroyed me. What is fantastic is that the people that are now in control seem to be turning it around.’.

There was a mood of cautious optimism from other fans. ‘I have been a fan since forever, well the 1980s at least,’ said Gavin Fullarton. ‘I have seen this team in every division. I have seen them in the downs and downs. But I think we are going in the right direction. So far.’.

Industry observers note that he added: ‘The upcoming guys seem to know what they are doing. They are communicative.’.

There were 1,216 fans in the ground on Saturday with 300 stalwarts travelling down from the north. Colin Richardson, an Accies supporter, was asked why so many had stuck by the club.

‘It’s about loyalty,’ he said. ‘You can’t pick and choose when you support your team. At the moment it is all about small steps. It has to be about stability.’.

Industry observers note that A Ross County fan had travelled up from North Wales. The journey to Scotland is a familiar one for Ian Ellson. ‘I have been all over Scotland to watch Ross County,’ he stated. ‘Twenty years ago I visited Ross County and I was spoiled rotten. I decided to follow them.’.

A social worker, he averages one visit a month. ‘I live and breathe Ross County,’ he remarked. ‘This season we are going up.’.

Welsh Staggies fan Ian Elson and Englishman Ray Griffiths travelled far for Saturday's game.

It has been revealed that brian Graham would not be so bullish. He is 39 this month and has learned enough about football to know that predictions are made only to make the speaker seem foolish down the line.

Recent findings suggest that he was, though, expansive about what is happening at County. He joined the club for the second time in the summer after Stuart Kettlewell, the manager, convinced him of the ambitions in Dingwall.

‘This is a club where I have had success before so I know how good a club it can be,’ he said. ‘It’s not been great for a couple of seasons but in the summer the manager set out his stall very early. It was about leaving egos at the door, building a togetherness and having a change of culture at the club. I think you are seeing that now.’.

The early signs were good for the striker who dropped down from Falkirk in the Premiership to play in Dingwall.

‘We had good pre-season performances against Aberdeen and Dundee and that was a solid building block,’ he remarked.

Brian Graham celebrates after scoring his 21st goal of the season for County.

Graham converted a first-half penalty to reach a tally of 21 goals this season and the Christmas trees are not up yet. ‘I get a lot of plaudits for scoring goals but others in the team are scoring a lot too,’ he remarked. ‘We are scoring team goals.’.

Has he set a target for the season? ‘When I came back I knew I had to score 13 to reach 50 goals for the club in two spells,’ he stated. ‘I always set down targets in a wee black book but now I might need to readjust that.’.

Industry observers note that it was a night of adjustment for Darian MacKinnon. He had set a victory target but was condemned to accept defeat. He would not concede the league race was over. ‘We have to play them twice,’ he said.

Industry observers note that he added ‘We are going in the right direction. The owners have put money in and they have backed us.’.

According to recent reports, asked to pinpoint a factor that has contributed to the team sitting second, he stated: ‘The most positive thing for me this season is that this is now a good place to come into your work after the last three or four seasons. We are all actually enjoying coming to our work.’.

There is work to be done on and off the pitch but the Accies are surviving. And that is the biggest result.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that 'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'.

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.
