💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.
  • Fortunately, we are still far from that point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026.

Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.

Fortunately, we are still far from that point. At 72, Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever. His eyes are perfectly good when bespectacled, his mind nimble enough to keep up with play and his soothingly familiar voice strong and authoritative with a gentle tendency towards self-deprecation.

This much was evident as Manchester United roared back to beat Roma in the Champions League and a clip of his spine-tingling commentary from the live CBS broadcast circulated on social media and found an appreciative audience in Europe.

Sources indicate that 'I don't know if there's an element of nostalgia in hearing my voice again,' says Tyldesley. 'If I'm honest, I've dodged the worst of the public's ire with everything including commentators because I haven't been around for the last few years.

In a recent development, 'Absence has made a few hearts grow a little fonder towards me and maybe if I'd been on Sky every week for the last six years, I'd be no less unpopular than anybody else out there. So, I can't pretend it's not nice to get some engagement with an audience I used to commentate to on a regular basis, but I'm very happy where I am.'.

Tyldesley has been the lead commentator for the CBS coverage of the Champions League since 2020, converting transfer fees into US dollars and keeping his measurements imperial for a North American audience but otherwise approaching the job as he always did.

Clive Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever at 72 and is 'very happy' in his role as the lead commentator of CBS coverage of the Champions League.

Tyldesley's commentary of Man United's comeback against Roma circulated on social media and received an appreciative audience in Europe.

The 72-year-old wonders whether there was an element of nostalgia to the reaction, with Tyldesley's work for CBS meaning his commentary cannot be shown in Europe.

Clips of the studio panel featuring Thierry Henry, Micah Richards, Jamie Carragher and presenter Kate Scott are popular on social media but live action featuring Tyldesley's commentary is governed by broadcasting rights deals and cannot be shown in Europe.

The one from Old Trafford of Matheus Cunha's winning goal in the 86th minute slipped through the net on X and reminded everyone his passion for football is undimmed, and his voice can still stand hairs on attention.

'I don't think I've seen a better game than the first leg of the Paris Saint-Germain v Bayern Munich Champions League semi-final,' notes Tyldesley on the rare quality of Europe's elite competition. 'I listened to people with hundreds more England caps than me saying it was bad defending, but I watched the whole game back the next day and it wasn't.

'I'm sorry but it was wonderful attacking and a show of intent by two coaches who trusted defenders to defend one-on-one and attackers to score more than the opposition. Rob Green was my co-commentator and at the end we just put our microphones down and looked at each other and said, "Wow.".

It has been revealed that 'I've not forgotten muddy pitches and assassin centre backs. You only need to look on YouTube to see football was different, but you can't pretend it was better. I see terrible games today just as I did then, but particularly in the Champions League, I regularly stumble upon football that gets me off my seat.'.

His exit from ITV, first displaced by Sam Matterface as lead commentator in 2020 and then released entirely after Euro 2024 clearly smarted but Tyldesley is comfortable as the veteran in the fast-changing media landscape.

'Most of the principles I picked up from watching John Motson, Barry Davies and Brian Moore in their pomp are applicable to commentary in 2026,' he indicates. 'There's no need to reinvent that particular wheel.

'You can offer alternatives such as fan zones and screaming watchalongs for people to view it in a different way. I make it my business to look at J_Tekkz or LDN Movements or whatever is pulling in millions on YouTube.

Tyldesley believes he has not seen a better game than the first leg of PSG's Champions League semi-final with Bayern Munich last year.

The veteran commentator believes most of the principles he learned starting out still apply, but admits to having watched popular new voices to see if anything could apply to his commentary.

Tyldesley also works as a guest lecturer and commentates for blockbuster computer games, as well as selling framed prints of his commentary charts.

'I sample a bit of Mark Goldbridge to see why he's prominent but I'm hearing nothing in those guys applicable to the way I call a football match so I carry on with the same focus I've always had on what constitutes good commentary.'.

The central principle being that the game is bigger than the individuals in it, he points out, with viewers tuning in for the football not the commentator.

'The biggest challenge for a television commentator is to find the right words at the big moments, to go beyond "amazing," "brilliant", "incredible" and try to add some editorial context,' indicates Tyldesley.

In a recent development, 'Every goal is unique. The words following a goal that is going to be remembered for years should be unique and specific to that goal, but that's difficult to do. It's unscripted performance and difficult to master and capture.

In a recent development, 'I am concentrating hardest for the 10-15 seconds after a substantial goal because I'm searching for words which will become a small part of people's memories. That's very different to consciously trying to provide 45-second soundbites to amplify one's own personality and standing on social media.

'There's a danger of media leaning that way as it develops such an emphasis on the bitesize.'.

Among other things, Tyldesley is a guest lecturer for media students at the University of Salford, still doing commentaries for blockbuster computer games and selling framed prints of his commentary charts, something that started as 'a silly idea in lockdown'.

Industry observers note that his wife Susan bought a dozen frames to see how it went. Originally, he offered three Champions League finals won by English clubs in 1999, 2005 and 2012. He sent one each to Gary Neville who played for Manchester United in 1999 and Jamie Carragher who played for Liverpool in 2005. They both posted images online and demand skyrocketed.

Sources indicate that 'Two good friends,' smiles Tyldesley. 'I probably got about half a million pounds of free advertising out of them.' Sales have soared beyond 50,000. There's a Celtic chart on the gym in Rod Stewart's house. Ant and Dec have bought signed Newcastle charts.

His own venture into podcasting was short-lived and he politely declines between five and ten invitations each week to appear on others.

Industry observers note that 'I've tried to step back from that kind of thing,' indicates Tyldesley. 'So much content I hear on football is empty, verbose and repetitive. Really, there are only so many things you can say about Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled in mid-air and Gary Neville probably stated most of them in the 30 seconds following the incident.

Tyldesley has no plans to retire and Paramount, the owners of his employers CBS - and soon to be the owners of TNT Sports - will have the UK rights for the Champions League.

Sales of his framed commentary charts, something that started during lockdown, have soared beyond 50,000.

'There are so many brutally judgmental loud voices in and around football attracting attention that I want to be as far away from as possible, so that's what I do. Unless I sense an opportunity to talk about communication and broadcasting rather than whether club A, B or C should replace their manager. That's not for me Clive.'.

So, there's a little less Tyldesley out there than there was. He was content to stay at home and watch the World Cup from his sofa this summer for the first time since 1990.

It has been revealed that but there are no plans to retire. And who knows what might change next season when Paramount, the owners of CBS – and soon to be the owners of current rights holders TNT Sports – have the UK rights for the Champions League.

There might be a familiar voice beamed into our living rooms once again.

When I saw the Dear England play, I was the only person in the theatre who didn't enjoy it, and that was because I hated the portrayal of Harry Kane.

He was written as an uneducated numbskull. Written to laugh at and the theatre laughed at him. He was stupid and gullible, another thick footballer.

And anyone who has spent time with footballers will know they might lack for an Eton College education but are streetwise and invariably smart with a razor sharp sense of humour.

According to recent reports, kane is a leader of those men. There's not a single thing about the person Kane has made himself to laugh or sneer at and I wanted to stand up in the theatre that afternoon and shout at everyone.

Oddly, I was introduced to the playwright James Graham at a function a few weeks later and he kind of pushed me for my opinion of Dear England.

I tried to be diplomatic, but I felt so strongly I ended up scolding him for writing a character called Harry Kane who was nothing like Harry Kane.

So, that was the end of a beautiful friendship before it began. And I'm so thrilled now there's a better appreciation of the person Harry is.

L'ex difensore commenta il primo posto dei biancocelesti e il lavoro del tecnico.

According to recent reports, ex difensore della Lazio e campione del mondo con l'Italia nel 2006, Massimo Oddo conosce bene sia l'ambiente biancoceleste sia Gennaro Gattuso, con cui ha condiviso lo spogliatoio al Milan e in Nazionale. In un'intervista a La Repubblica, l'ex terzino ha parlato del primo posto della Lazio e del lavoro svolto dal tecnico.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that rino riforma gli spogliatoi dove comanda. Prima da calciatore, ora da tecnico, ha sempre avuto la capacità di rieducare senza punire, riabilitando anche i contesti più critici. È un po’ lo stesso senso del carcere, nel senso più virtuoso del termine. Scherzi a parte, l’impennata della Lazio non è un caso, ma il frutto degli insegnamenti di Gattuso. Rino rieducava senza mai punire: bastavano due minuti di ritardo e scattava il rimprovero. Non serviva l’intervento della società. Non finge mai, anche se in questi giorni ripete spesso una bugia: ‘Non guardo la classifica’. Sta guidando la Lazio oltre il potenziale della sua rosa. Può restare in alto fino alla fine.

Mi emoziono, sono felicissimo di vederla in testa al campionato. Guardo Nuno Tavares e Floriani e rivedo il mio passato. Viviamo una situazione unica: da una parte la gioia per il risultato, dall’altra la sofferenza dei tifosi che rinunciano allo stadio. Mi auguro che si trovi una soluzione, perché da ex capitano conosco l’amore, immenso e indispensabile, del popolo laziale.

Gattuso non cambia, migliora. Da ct, mancando la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha subito una delle lezioni sportive più grandi della sua carriera, non solo per il risultato. Adesso ha preso ancora più consapevolezza di prima, ma è sempre stato un ‘braccio armato’ pronto a intervenire e risolvere i momenti di crisi.

Industry observers note that la sosta di Campionato ha visto diversi rossoneri impegnati con le loro Nazionali. Le prestazioni sono state nel complesso positive: Rabiot e Maignan, pur senza brillare, si sono qualificati con la loro Francia per i quarti di finale di Nations League; qualche preoccupazione per il nostro portierone che ha riportato un infortunio all’anca, che tuttavia non dovrebbe impedirgli di giocare contro il Frosinone. Molto bene Diego Moreira, tra i protagonisti, segnando anche un goal nella lezione impartita dal Belgio agli azzurri. Qualche ombra arriva invece da Gonçalo Ramos, rimasto a digiuno con il Portogallo, già qualificato ai quarti, sia nella partita casalinga con la Danimarca (i danesi hanno vinto 4-1 e Gonçalo non ha toccato un pallone nel cuore della difesa avversaria), sia nella trasferta in Galles (vittoria 3-2 per gli uomini di Jorge Jesus). Il suo collega di reparto, Francesco Camarda è invece andato in goal con l’Under 21 nell’amichevole con i pari età francesi, un’iniezione di fiducia per il prodotto del nostro vivaio in attesa di sapere quale sarà il suo destino nel mercato invernale. Anche Christian Pulisic torna ulteriormente rinfrancato dopo il doppio confronto tra USA e Haiti (certo non così probante), grazie ai due goal segnati nella prima gara, cui ha fatto seguito il bellissimo goal in rovesciata nella seconda.

Qualche parola in più, tuttavia, voglio spenderla su Alphadjo Cisse che, a vent’anni appena compiuti, dopo 14 presenze nell’U21, ha fatto il suo esordio con la Nazionale italiana nella partita contro il Belgio. Un’esperienza che non ho mai avuto la gioia di vivere ma che immagino come qualcosa di indimenticabile o, se preferite, unforgettable (J). Una carica di energia e consapevolezza che - ne sono certo - il ragazzo saprà utilizzare a favore della squadra, dove peraltro ha già segnato a ripetizione fra campionato e Coppa.

Recent findings suggest that nel suo debutto azzurro, Alphadjo è subentrato a Scalvini al 17’ della ripresa con la squadra sotto per 3-1, non certo il migliore dei contesti. Il suo approccio è stato perfetto: ha mostrato la solita naturalezza e ha provato a rendersi subito protagonista con il gesto tecnico che, per quanto prevedibile, è difficile da neutralizzare: il destro a giro sul palo lontano della porta avversaria scoccato in prossimità del vertice sinistro dell’area, un’esecuzione che ha procurato il rigore poi fallito da Pio Esposito.

Ma chi è Alphadjo, calcisticamente? Come si sa, gli osservatori del Milan lo seguivano da tempo e lo hanno intercettato ufficialmente a metà dello scorso campionato, quando, in prestito dal Verona, stava giocando in serie B al Catanzaro, sotto la guida di Alberto Aquilani. Quando ormai la sua partenza in direzione PSV Eindhoven sembrava decisa, la società rossonera si è inserita e se lo è assicurato per una cifra attorno ai 10 milioni, lasciandolo a Catanzaro fino a fine stagione. Un grave infortunio nel febbraio di quest’anno lo ha tenuto lontano dalle competizioni fino alla scorsa estate gettando enormi dubbi sul suo completo recupero. Invece il ragazzo nato in provincia di Treviso è tornato in campo ancora più determinato, a dimostrazione di come il talento abbia bisogno di motivazione e resilienza per emergere. Si pensava che potesse passare dal Milan Futuro, e invece Amorim se ne è innamorato (indimenticabile quel “I love Cisse”, subito dopo aver dichiarato di non voler parlare di singoli giocatori): e il suo pupillo lo ha ricambiato andando subito in gol (destro a girare partendo da sinistra, of course) nell’esordio contro il Torino.

Il nostro numero 70, alto 1,78 per una settantina di chili, dotato di gambe molto forti che gli permettono di dribblare, di difendere la palla e di vincere contrasti, può giocare in diversi ruoli o, meglio, svolgere diverse funzioni: seconda punta, mezzala, trequartista ed esterno. Credo che da esterno, sul lato sinistro del campo, possa esprimersi al meglio perché può rientrare dentro al campo e tentare la “sua” giocata, di cui abbiamo già parlato. Cisse ha comunque un’abilità nella lettura degli spazi in cui può ricevere palla che gli permette di seguire lo sviluppo del gioco e di essere efficace in ogni situazione: intelligente, ad esempio, il suo movimento a occupare lo spazio lasciato libero da Gonçalo Ramos, che a sua volta determina quello dei difendenti rossoblù, per trovare l’impatto con la palla, servitagli da Pulisic, per il goal del vantaggio rossonero a Marassi, nell’ultima gara prima della sosta. Abbastanza impressionante anche la tripletta in Europa League contro il Salisburgo, con gol di testa, di destro e di sinistro, tutti segnati nell’area piccola dimostrando anche un grande opportunismo da prima punta. Qualcosa in più forse dovrà dare in fase difensiva dal punto di vista attentivo, ma la cosiddetta “self regulation”, cioè l’attitudine a volersi migliorare in allenamento e in partita, col tempo lo aiuterà a crescere anche nei compiti senza palla.

In a recent development, non dimentichiamoci che il ragazzo è il nostro capocannonierecon 8 goal, di cui 5 in campionato in 9 presenze, per un totale di 407 minuti (5 da titolare e 4 da subentrato). Non male per un ventenne. Da domenica ci attende un tour de force di 7 partite in 28 giorni, ci sarà bisogno di tutti e avremo bisogno che Alpha, così lo chiamano compagni ed amici, continui a stupire!

Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026.

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their latest head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

It has been revealed that frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington mentioned the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington stated: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'.

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

In a recent development, pfannenstiel said: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their fresh manager.

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'.

Recent findings suggest that before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

Industry observers note that as a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

According to recent reports, frick stated: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'.

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

E come tale deve agire nel contesto territoriale in cui siamo ma anche nel resto del mondo cercando di fare del bene e rendere felici i meno fortunati. Attenzione al terzo settore, abbiamo tre squadre special: i primi attori sono i calciatori, loro non se ne rendono conto ma con le loro gesta sono una fonte di felicità. By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:49 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 15 November 2026.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

Bacher, 30, essentially failed to let go of the ball at the right time, leaving his team-mates stunned.

The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

Arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

Industry observers note that "Están matando al fútbol"Por el "insólito" gol en contra que se hace el arquero de Comunicaciones ante Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/GLUJlcKPXK.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored a bizarre own goal during his side's third-tier play-off game.

The 30-year-old failed to release the ball from a throw and launched the ball into his own net.

Fans flooded to social media to react to the scarcely believable own goal.

One wrote on X: 'Haha, those who think it's because of betting. That's the level of Argentine football.'.

Another posted: 'RIP Argentinian football.'.

Industry observers note that A third shared: 'The Arsenal lot celebrating... you've got some nerve.'.

Bacher joined the club at the start of last year, but has always played in his homeland of Argentina.

His Comunicaciones side finished ninth in their league group of Primera B, the third tier of Argentinian football, and were taken on by an Arsenal side that came second.

They will face off in the return leg next Saturday.

Liverpool must make January signing after telling Trey Nyoni comments

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.
  • The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).
  • However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.

The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).

However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.

It’s reassuring that links to Lamine Camara (who came close to a switch to Chelsea in the summer) have resurfaced ahead of the winter, given ongoing concerns over how Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch fit in an Andoni Iraola side.

While the performances of Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni have undoubtedly mitigated matters, the truth of the matter is that Liverpool can’t look to rely on the latter of the duo throughout an entire campaign.

The Reds must, and no doubt will, look after the teenager to ensure his excellent development carries on smoothly, but his recent comments are a clear reminder that investment midway through the campaign is a necessity.

“I’ve been playing like a number six. I played there when I was young but, to be honest, it’s a new position for me. I’ve had to learn a lot in a short space of time,” Nyoni told The Inside Scoop (via BBC Sport).

“I enjoy playing like a six because I can get on the ball and always try to play forwards, but I enjoy playing as an eight as well.

“I like to drop in, get the ball and play forward but I’ve had to learn the discipline of being a number six.

“Right now, I don’t really have a preference. As I’m starting out, I enjoy playing both.”.

According to recent reports, we have faith that Iraola’s demands will eventually click with Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, but it’s still painful to see how open Liverpool look in the middle of the park when Mac Allister is forced to share space with either of his senior midfield partners. And the less noted about a double pivot consisting of the Dutchman and the Hungarian, the better.

Yes, it’s fair to point out that our season is far from spiralling under Iraola — the Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table with only four points standing between them and Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Brighton in second.

According to recent reports, but it does feel like there is an opportunity for Liverpool to make a modest statement in 2026/27. Not quite title glory, it has to be said, but certainly to stake a claim as “best of the rest” and set a promising foundation for the seasons to come under Iraola.

Adding an additional midfielder (like, cough cough, Lamine Camara, cough cough) to the ranks who can carry out the Basque’s demands would undoubtedly serve that purpose.

Elsewhere, the backline looks in fine shape and the forward line evidently needs time to gel. Give the manager the tools he needs in midfield and this could be an impressive opening campaign for Andoni Iraola.

  • Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar announced his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.

Having enjoyed retirement for 11 years, he shocked world football by agreeing a surprise transfer to Serie C outfit Ravenna, where he was set to undertake a marketing role.

It was initially understood that he would not be making a playing return, but the Brazil legend laced up his boots on Sunday and played a part in his side's opening goal.

Ravenna's honorary vice president Ariedo Braida said in June that the World Cup winner would regrettably not be able to play for the club due to his age.

But it appears that went up in smoke, with Ronaldinho playing 45 minutes on his return in the league clash – despite his move being dubbed a publicity stunt by the club.

Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46.

He played the first-half of the game, playing a role in the first goal for his newly introduced side.

He helped set up Giulio Donati's opening goal of the match, and raced across the field to mob the goal scorer as he celebrated.

In a recent development, he started the game, playing the first-half before being replaced by Matteo Maggio. Before his substitution, he embraced the fans in the stands at the interval.

The icon hinted there could be more games to come, however.

He told Sky Italia after the game: 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me.

'Is this my last one? I don't know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.

Sources indicate that 'It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.'.

Ronaldinho has also become a shareholder in the club.

During his illustrious career, he won the World Cup, a Champions League, two LaLiga titles and a Serie A trophy before hanging up his boots in 2015.

He also won a string of individual accolades including the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005.

Nella Serie A 2025-26 l’olandese aveva segnato quattro reti in 29 presenze; ora conta anche quattro assist.

Tijjani Noslin ha segnato quattro gol e servito quattro assist con la Lazio: per partecipazioni alle reti in Serie A è secondo solo ad Adrien Rabiot. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Il francese del Milan conta cinque gol e quattro assist, uno in più dell’olandese nel totale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that noslin ha realizzato le sue quattro reti in 10 partite di campionato. Sono tante quante quelle segnate nelle 29 presenze dell’intera Serie A 2025-26. Solo una volta ha fatto meglio, arrivando a cinque gol nella stagione 2023-24.

Il suo percorso da rider a realizzatore si è sviluppato nell’arco di cinque anni, dal 2021 a oggi, passando attraverso difficoltà e successi. Ora i suoi gol e i suoi assist lo collocano tra i giocatori più incisivi del campionato, non soltanto della Lazio.

Il dato più alto di Noslin per partecipazioni alle reti in una stagione di Serie A resta quello del 2023-24. Con l’Hellas Verona, in 17 partite, fu coinvolto in nove gol: cinque segnati e quattro assist.

Con i quattro gol e i quattro assist attuali è a quota otto. Ha dunque già eguagliato il numero di passaggi decisivi registrato in quella stagione, mentre gli manca una partecipazione a una rete per raggiungerne il totale.

Striker Che Adams indicates Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is big on the small details... 'he loves his FaceTime calls'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be major on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the new man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Striker Adams indicates Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

Industry observers note that hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

Sources indicate that ‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

In a recent development, john McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

According to recent reports, ‘He mentioned to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very notable to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ said Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

It has been revealed that ‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.

Mercoledì 25 novembre, l'Inter ospita a San Siro lo Stoccarda per provare a vincere e continuare a marciare nella speranza di agguantare un posto fra le prime otto nella League Phase di Champions League.

"La vittoria in Olanda sul Feyenoord ha sistemato un bel po’ di cose in casa Inter, però, per alimentare il sogno di un arrivo nelle prime otto e sostenere un più realistico pass per gli spareggi, Cristian Chivu deve battere lo Stoccarda, perché poi avrà due tapponi, Borussia Dortmund e Liverpool. Il piano è semplice: tre punti contro lo Stoccarda mercoledì e tre a Bratislava contro lo Slovan il 27 gennaio per garantirsi i 12 punti necessari per i playoff, e vada come vada contro il Borussia e il Liverpool. Lo Stoccarda non è un ostacolo insormontabile, in Bundesliga galleggia all’ottavo posto. In Champions però è 14°, un gradino sopra l’Inter, 7 punti contro 6, e non verrà a San Siro in gita scolastica".

In a recent development, "È una squadra molesta in senso buono, pressa e fa girare il pallone con scaltrezza. Angelo Stiller, formatosi nel Bayern, funge da piede perno, dirige il gioco. Sia il Milan sia l’Inter hanno chiesto informazioni sul suo conto. Stiller però si è fatto male a fine ottobre, un infortunio muscolare da cui è quasi guarito, ma quel “quasi” pesa. «Servirà un recupero al fotofinish», ha detto l’allenatore Sebastian Hoeness, nipote di Uli Hoeness, grande attaccante del Bayern anni Settanta e poi presidente del club. In avanti attenzione al curdo-tedesco Deniz Undav, un predatore in evidenza nella Germania al Mondiale con tre gol, uno a Curaçao e due alla Costa d’Avorio. Molto dipenderà dalla presenza o meno di Stiller".

(Fonte: La Gazzetta dello Sport).

Le ultime dai campi e le probabili formazioni di Juventus-Venezia:.

La Juventus, dopo la sosta per le nazionali, è pronta a tornare in campo in campionato per sfidare il Venezia domenica alle 12:30. Contro i lagunari Spalletti si affiderà al 3-4-2-1: in porta ci sarà Vicario. In difesa spazio a Gatti, Bremer e Lucumì. A centrocampo sulla destra giocherà McKennie, in mezzo spazio a Douglas Luiz e Koopmeiners, mentre a sinistra è toccherà a Cabal. Sulla trequarti sarà confermato Alajbegovic che avrà al suo fianco Kolo Muani. Entrambi giocheranno alle spalle di Woltemade. Nelle ore che precederanno la partita Luciano Spalletti proverà a recuperare tre giocatori, almeno per la panchina: i nomi sono quelli di Nico Gonzalez, Zeki Celic e Andrea Cambiaso. (da Torino, Camillo Demichelis).

Industry observers note that yeboah è l’ultimo a rientrare dei nazionali e Nicola studia l’ipotesi di riproporre la doppia punta a Torino, con Lauberbach al fianco di Adams. In mezzo ballottaggio fra Basic e Busio per affiancare Kike Perez e Sohm, con Hainaut e Mazzocchi esterni del 3-5-2. Davanti a Stankovic scalpita Bella-Kotchap, ma dovrebbero essere confermati Halhal, Moreno e Juan Jesus in difesa. (da Venezia, Daniele Najjar).

#61443. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

📅 04 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5263 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago.
  • Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025.
  • If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

It has been revealed that “With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

In a recent development, quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

Recent findings suggest that the next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still highlighted great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

It has been revealed that “I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

It has been revealed that “He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw.

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We demonstrated that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”.

He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

It has been revealed that szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

In a recent development, mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

Sources indicate that A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an key clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

In a recent development, fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

It has been revealed that lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

According to recent reports, szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

According to recent reports, isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

In a recent development, emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

According to recent reports, another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Sources indicate that inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

Sources indicate that liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

According to recent reports, wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

We are under way at Portman Road.

It has been revealed that both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Palacios, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.Substitutes: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Ouattara, Florentino, Nunez, McAteer, Clarke, Flemming.

Liverpool: Alisson; Jacquet, Araujo, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Munoz, Isak, Gakpo.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Barcola, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Koumas, Ngumoha.

According to recent reports, "Everyone's going to love him" 😍Jamie Redknapp is looking forward to seeing Bradley Barcola play for Liverpool this evening! pic.twitter.com/Ut9Zx4gbB2.

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

Industry observers note that "He is the talisman already inside these first two games"Can Julio Enciso provide another assist tonight? 👀 pic.twitter.com/FaDkndt3BG.

"I'm desperate for him to do well!" Jamie Redknapp says Florian Wirtz has to produce more for Liverpool right now 💭 pic.twitter.com/1fYT9t9tx3.

A milestone appearance for Dom 🫰🔴 pic.twitter.com/C28iemsxou.

"I really feel they've got that recruitment right' Luke Chambers says the Premier League experience of players that Ipswich have signed will be massive for them 🧠 pic.twitter.com/DgwYsTlHBD.

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”.

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

A first Reds start for Ronald 💪 pic.twitter.com/P80pwhlBJ9.

"He's ready, definitely we will use him in the second half" Andoni Iraola says Bradley Barcola has looked good in training and is hoping to give him some game time against Ipswich ⏳ pic.twitter.com/C00WVI7ACd.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the right now injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:.

According to recent reports, we are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola remarked. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

Sources indicate that “He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

It has been revealed that ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil remarked. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

Industry News: Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admits his newlook team need to deliver sooner rather than later

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a fresh style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

Sources indicate that asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he remarked: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  notes his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'.

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

Industry observers note that ‘Some newly introduced faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’.

McGinn also remarked that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most vital part.

Sources indicate that ‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

In a recent development, ‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’.

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager stated: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’.

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

Industry observers note that but the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

According to recent reports, ‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

In a recent development, ‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

It has been revealed that ‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’.
